s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic progressive vascular skin lesions with neurological and familial components
salient_findings: Bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Female patient in her early 50s
Multiple skin lesions on the lower legs
Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Lesions bleed occasionally after trauma
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
History of intracranial hemorrhage
Recurrent seizures at age 4
Lipolymphedema of the lower legs due to functional venous insufficiency
Wearing compression stockings for years
Family history of similar conditions
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography showed intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed dilated venous-like malformations with thrombosis
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

shortlist.label: Cerebral cavernous malformations
shortlist.why_kept: KRIT1 variant detected, matches family history of intracranial hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions and vascular malformations match clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Family history and vascular malformations are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Lipolymphedema and vascular malformations are characteristic of this condition

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Neurological symptoms and vascular malformations are plausible for this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, a history of intracranial hemorrhage, and skin lesions consistent with vascular malformations support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of specific mention of arteriovenous malformations

rejected.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
rejected.why: Typically presents with mucocutaneous telangiectasias and recurrent epistaxis, not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by port-wine stains, varicose veins, and bony or soft tissue hypertrophy, which are not the primary features in this case

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with a port-wine stain in the distribution of the trigeminal nerve, not consistent with the patient's presentation
